approach: audio-analyzer-rs MCP tool: full_analysis (section boundaries) -> LLM clustering + rhythm_analysis time series
note: MOV not supported by Symphonia — audio extracted to FLAC first via ffmpeg

song_boundaries.evidence: Harmonic cascade (11:20–12:37) after energy+texture cluster. Harmonic-only boundaries = new key = new song. Aligns with Exp02 estimate of 11:30.
Confidence 0.97 (spectral+texture) within cluster starting at 32:13 (0.77). Followed by 0.98 at 38:27. Two consecutive near-maximum multi-feature boundaries. Aligns with Exp02 estimate of 33:30.

Confidence 1.00 (maximum in entire recording, energy+spectral+texture). Immediately followed by longest sustained quiet stretch (~7 min, 45:59–53:07). Strongest song-boundary signal in the dataset. NOT found by Exp02.
Confidence 0.90 (spectral+texture). Followed by two consecutive 5-min quiet stretches (55:37–60:35, 60:42–65:31). No energy component weakens case slightly.
Confidence 0.91 (energy+spectral+texture). All three feature types. Dense surrounding cluster (65:31–70:31) reduces certainty.

onset_strength_quiet_zones.note: ~5 min quiet inside Song 5 — possible additional boundary or long breakdown

findings: MCP section boundaries are intra-song (163 in 95 min = ~35s each), same class as allin1's 256 segments
LLM clustering of MCP boundaries is fast and effective — no additional API calls needed beyond the clustering call
Harmonic cascade boundaries (consecutive harmonic-only changes) are a strong signal for key changes = song transitions

The 1.00 confidence boundary at 45:59 + longest quiet stretch is the clearest song boundary in the dataset — gap score (Exp02) completely missed it because playing style in the second half masks it as an energy dip
MCP onset time series confirms all 5 boundaries and reveals a 5-min quiet zone at 60-65 min that may be an additional boundary
MOV container unsupported by Symphonia — need ffmpeg to extract to FLAC as preprocessing step
